name: K R Nagarajan
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Ramraj Cotton (Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu)
profile: Tiruppur entrepreneur who founded Ramraj Khadi Traders in 1983 to sell dhotis and support local weavers; renamed Ramraj Cotton in 1987. Built it into India's leading dhoti/veshti and white-shirt ethnic-wear brand, with 250+ stores by its 40th anniversary in 2023 and exports to Sri Lanka, Singapore and Malaysia.
interesting_fact: The 'Ramraj' name combines letters from his own name (Nagarajan) and his father's (Ramaswamy); the business began with just a table and a chair in a small Tirupur office.
deep_cut_fact: He finished his SSLC in 1977 but couldn't afford college, so went straight to work, spending 18 months at a Tirupur dhoti maker learning production and marketing; being stopped by a hotel watchman for wearing a dhoti later inspired the brand's 'Salute Ramraj' pride-in-dhoti positioning.
notes: Company contact page lists only customer care/franchise/corporate-orders emails, no press contact. Tamil-language interview (Vikatan, 2020) says he started trading at age 13.

name: Zheng Xiukang
current_role: Deceased (founder of Kangnai Group, Wenzhou); died 20 April 2022 aged 76
profile: Founder of Kangnai (康奈) Group, one of China's best-known leather-shoe makers, from Wenzhou. Died 20 April 2022 aged 76, as announced by his daughter and reported by Jiemian/Tianxia Wangshang.
interesting_fact: Started shoemaking only at 33 as an apprentice; founded the 'Red Elephant' shoe workshop in 1980, which became Kangnai, and was called one of China's two 'shoe kings' alongside Aokang's Wang Zhentao.
notes: Deceased (April 2022) - source: https://www.jiemian.com/article/7361425.html. Remaining fields skipped per instructions.

name: Vijaykumar Taparia
current_role: Executive (Whole-time) Director, The Supreme Industries Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: V.K. Taparia is a member of the Taparia family that controls The Supreme Industries, India's largest plastics processor (piping systems, moulded furniture, packaging films, industrial products). A B.Com graduate, he has been on Supreme's board since October 1984 and was re-appointed Executive Director at the 2026 AGM with his term running to Sept 2027.
interesting_fact: He has sat on Supreme Industries' board for over four decades (appointed 29 Oct 1984) and personally holds about 244,890 Supreme shares per the 2025-26 annual report.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Company is fronted by Chairman & MD M.P. Taparia, so outreach via the company (registered office Raheja Chambers, Nariman Point, Mumbai) is the realistic route.

current_role: Listed by Hurun China (2003) as owner of Minglun Group; current role not verified
profile: Appears on the 2003 Hurun China list (about US$120M) with wealth attributed to Minglun Group (electronics, trade, food processing). No public sources could be found confirming his biography or current activity.

name: J Murugavel
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Matrimony.com Ltd (BharatMatrimony), Chennai
profile: Murugavel Janakiraman studied statistics at Presidency College Chennai and did an MCA at the University of Madras. While working as a software consultant in New Jersey he started a Tamil community portal in April 1997, which became TamilMatrimony and then BharatMatrimony (2000). He built Matrimony.com into India's largest matchmaking group, listed in 2017, and still runs it.
interesting_fact: The company's own board page says he found his wife through his own matchmaking site.
deep_cut_fact: Matrimony.com began as a hobby: a community portal for Tamil NRIs that he built in his spare time in New Jersey in 1997. The matrimonial listings on that portal took off and became TamilMatrimony. He is also Chairman Emeritus of IAMAI (Internet and Mobile Association of India).
notes: Full name Murugavel Janakiraman. Accessible founder who often speaks to the Indian business press; the corporate communications email is the best route. No verified personal social accounts were confirmed.

name: Jamie Iannone
current_role: President & CEO, eBay Inc. (since April 2020)
profile: Princeton BS/Stanford MBA; started at Booz Allen and Epinions, led search and buyer experience at eBay (2001-09), ran NOOK at Barnes & Noble, then was CEO of SamsClub.com and COO of Walmart eCommerce. CEO of eBay since April 2020; in 2026 he closed the Depop deal and the board rejected GameStop's unsolicited bid.
interesting_fact: At Walmart eCommerce he was responsible for Store No. 8, Walmart's in-house incubation hub. At Barnes & Noble he ran everything NOOK, from devices and software to digital content.
deep_cut_fact: His favourite eBay experience was selling a Hammond B-3 organ he had owned since he was a teenager to a church. When it arrived, the pastor sent a video of the organist playing it, and Iannone joked it never sounded that good when he played it.
notes: Press releases name Sybille St. Arromand as media relations and John Egbert as IR. He is a high-profile CEO, so go through eBay media relations. Good podcast angles: recommerce, AI in marketplaces, small business.

name: Denise Aguiar Alvarez
current_role: Director-General, Fundação Bradesco; external member of the Board of Directors, Banco Bradesco
profile: Eldest granddaughter of Bradesco founder Amador Aguiar. An educator (PUC pedagogy, NYU master's in education), she has led Fundação Bradesco since 1986 and sits on Bradesco's board. The foundation, Brazil's largest private social-investment programme, runs 40 schools in every state for 42,000+ students.
interesting_fact: Fundação Bradesco has invested about R$9.5bn in education over 10 years, about R$1.4bn in 2024 alone, and runs 40 schools across all Brazilian states.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the foundation she worked a year as a teacher and teaching aide in early-childhood education, helping students who had fallen behind. When her grandfather wanted her to take over, she agreed on one condition: that nobody should know she was his granddaughter during her first year.
notes: Also listed as Denise Aguiar Alvarez Valente. Previously chaired Todos Pela Educação and GIFE's governance council. Education and philanthropy is the natural angle. Route via Fundação Bradesco or Bradesco IR. Sources disagree on when she joined the board (1986 vs 1990).

name: Chang Zhaohua
current_role: Founder of MicroPort Scientific. Stepped down as CEO in April 2026 and resigned as chairman/director in October 2026; one report says he remains chief scientific officer.
profile: Shandong-born engineer (b. 1963) trained in cryogenic engineering in Shanghai, with a PhD from SUNY. He was a cryosurgery R&D executive in the US before founding MicroPort in Shanghai's Zhangjiang park in 1998. He built it into one of China's largest high-end medical-device groups and led it for about 28 years. He handed the CEO role to Jonathan Chen in 2026 and left the board in October 2026.
interesting_fact: MicroPort's first product, launched in 1999, was China's first domestically made PTCA balloon dilatation catheter, built in a small plant in Shanghai's Zhangjiang park.
deep_cut_fact: Before MicroPort he spent 1990-95 at Cryomedical Sciences in the US, rising from senior engineer to chief scientist and head of R&D, then was VP of R&D at Endocare (1996-97). His early degrees were in refrigeration and cryogenic engineering, and he still holds a professorship at the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology.
notes: Sensitive timing: he left the MicroPort board on 25 Oct 2026 amid a governance review (per Reuters/Bamboo Works), so avoid that topic. Medtech innovation and the cryo-engineering background are safer angles. No published press email was found. He is also a vice chairman of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce.

name: Eric B Stang
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Ooma Inc. (NYSE: OOMA); Director, Rambus
profile: Stanford economics AB and Harvard MBA who worked at McKinsey, Monitor Company and Raychem. As CEO of Lexar Media (2001-06) he grew it into a Silicon Valley public company with more than $850M in revenue, then ran medtech firm Reliant Technologies. He has led Ooma since 2009, taking it public on the NYSE. In 2026 the company is pushing Ooma AI with revenue growing about 25% a year.
interesting_fact: He grew flash-memory maker Lexar from a small private company into one of the 50 largest public tech companies in Silicon Valley before it became part of Micron.
deep_cut_fact: Outside work he lists sailing, skiing, backpacking and car racing among his hobbies. Before running companies he did stints at McKinsey, Monitor Company and Raychem.
notes: Also on the Avalanche Technology (MRAM) board, which is relevant to a data-center/memory angle. Ooma's published IR/press email could not be retrieved (Business Wire blocked), so use the Ooma investor relations site.

name: Gilbert L. Baird Iii
current_role: Managing Partner, GreyLion (New York middle-market growth equity firm); former director of TheRealReal (2018 to Nov 2025)
profile: Gilbert 'Chip' Baird III is a private equity investor. He started in Merrill Lynch investment banking, then worked at The Beacon Group and was a partner at Weston Presidio. In 2012 he co-founded PWP Growth Equity at Perella Weinberg, which spun out as GreyLion in 2020 and which he co-leads with David Ferguson. He sat on TheRealReal's board from 2018 until November 2025.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Perella Weinberg's growth equity strategy and led its 2020 spin-out into an independent firm, GreyLion. He has served on the boards of more than 20 portfolio companies.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his private-equity career at The Beacon Group he focused on business and industrial services, energy and general manufacturing companies. He holds a BS in Finance and International Business from Penn State.
notes: Goes by 'Chip'. He resigned from TheRealReal's board on 17 Nov 2025 but consulted for the company through June 2026. GreyLion's general inbox is the best route.

name: Michael Torok
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Director, JEC Capital Partners; non-executive director, Amarin Corp (since April 2025)
profile: Boston College-trained finance professional (BS Accounting & Finance, MS Finance) who began at PricewaterhouseCoopers, then was CFO of semiconductor-equipment firm Integrated Dynamics Engineering until its sale to Aalberts. Since 2008 he has run JEC Capital Partners, a US/German investment firm. As an engaged shareholder he joined Amarin's board in April 2025 after pushing for a strategic review.
interesting_fact: He joined Amarin's board in April 2025, shortly after JEC and Bradley Radoff, together holding about 15 million shares, publicly urged the board to start a strategic review.
deep_cut_fact: Before investing full-time he was CFO (2006-09) of Integrated Dynamics Engineering, a semiconductor equipment technology company later acquired by Aalberts Industries. He has also sat on the board of Liberated Syndication (Libsyn), a podcast hosting and monetisation platform, since December 2022.
notes: Low public profile, activist-style investor. The Libsyn board seat is a natural podcast hook (the Libsyn detail comes from secondary profiles such as fintool/MarketScreener). No published email was found for JEC Capital or Amarin IR.

name: Lange Bob De
current_role: Group President, Services, Distribution & Digital, Caterpillar Inc.; Director, AGCO Corp (since Jan 2021)
profile: Bob De Lange is a Belgian-trained mechanical engineer who joined Caterpillar in 1993 and held product and leadership roles in Europe and Asia, including VP of the Excavation Division (Singapore, 2015). He ran Construction Industries, a roughly $20bn business, from 2017, and since 2018 has led Caterpillar's dealer network, services and Cat Digital. He also sits on AGCO's board.
interesting_fact: He is responsible for the Caterpillar brand, its global dealer network and Cat Digital, the unit behind connected-machine data across Caterpillar's fleet.
deep_cut_fact: He earned both a BS and an MS in Mechanical Engineering from the Catholic University of Leuven (KU Leuven) in Belgium in 1992, then an MBA from EDHEC in France in 1993, the year he joined Caterpillar.
notes: Name order in the source is reversed ('Lange Bob De'). Still listed as a Caterpillar group president per the officers page and a Jan 2026 Form 4. Caterpillar's power-generation and data-center gensets business sits in a different segment, but the services/digital angle is relevant. No published press email could be retrieved (site blocks bots); use Caterpillar media relations via caterpillar.com.

name: Robert H Niehaus
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Iridium Communications; Founder & Co-Managing Partner, GCP Capital Partners; Director, Zeta Global
profile: Private-equity veteran: 17 years at Morgan Stanley merchant banking, then built Greenhill Capital Partners from 2000, renamed GCP Capital Partners in 2009. On Iridium's board since 2008 and chairman since 2009 (briefly CEO in 2009); now chairs it into a ~$8bn sale to Rocket Lab announced June 2026.
interesting_fact: Iridium became public through Greenhill's SPAC, GHL Acquisition Corp., which acquired Iridium Holdings in Sept 2009. Niehaus briefly served as CEO that year and has chaired the satellite operator ever since, through the SpaceX-launched Iridium NEXT constellation and the 2026 Rocket Lab deal.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Harvard Business School with high distinction as a Baker Scholar, after a BA in International Affairs from Princeton's Woodrow Wilson School.
notes: Strong angle for a podcast on space, connectivity and data infrastructure: Iridium's satellite network and the Rocket Lab acquisition, expected to close mid-2027. Iridium IR is listed as Kenneth Levy. He keeps a low personal media profile.

name: James A Mitarotonda
current_role: Founder, Chairman, President & CEO, Barington Capital Group; Director (former Chairman) of The Eastern Company
profile: New York activist investor who founded Barington Capital Group in January 2000. Barington takes stakes in undervalued public companies and pushes for strategy, operations and governance changes. He has sat on the boards of Avon, Pep Boys, Griffon, A. Schulman and others, and became chairman of The Eastern Company, a Connecticut industrial firm, in 2016. Barington is a 10%+ holder in Eastern.
interesting_fact: He has been a director of more than ten public companies, including Avon Products, Pep Boys, The Jones Group, Griffon, Gerber Scientific and Register.com.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in operating jobs at Bloomingdale's and Citibank before co-founding the brokerage Commonwealth Associates, where he was Chairman and co-CEO. He is a Queens College economics graduate and has served on the Queens College Board of Trustees.
notes: Barington's current bio lists him only as a director of Eastern, so his chairmanship may have ended; verify in Eastern's latest proxy. Some aggregators wrongly date Barington to 1991; the firm says January 2000. Queens College trustee detail is from the 2015 Eastern release (talent4boards).

name: Brian G Robins
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Snowflake Inc. (since Sept 2025); previously CFO of GitLab (2020-25)
profile: Nashville-educated finance executive (BS Finance, Lipscomb; MBA, Vanderbilt Owen) and serial software CFO at VeriSign, AlienVault, Cylance and Sisense. As GitLab's CFO from 2020 he took it through its 2021 IPO and roughly 450% revenue growth. In September 2025 he succeeded Mike Scarpelli as CFO of Snowflake, the AI Data Cloud company.
interesting_fact: He has served as CFO of six technology companies (VeriSign, AlienVault, Cylance, Sisense, GitLab and Snowflake). At GitLab, revenue rose about 450% during his tenure while he built operating leverage.
deep_cut_fact: Much of his CFO career was in cybersecurity (VeriSign, AlienVault, Cylance). He still sits on the Advisory Council of ForgePoint Capital, a cybersecurity VC, and chairs the audit committee of identity-verification company ID.me.
notes: Also listed on Brighton Park Capital's team page (advisor network). Strong fit for data-center and AI infrastructure economics. Route via Snowflake PR (Eszter Szikora, Head of PR) or IR (Katherine McCracken).

name: James Pursley
current_role: President, Hinge Health, Inc. (NYSE: HNGE)
profile: Jim Pursley is a digital-health commercial executive. After roles at GE Healthcare and Intel-GE Care Innovations, he joined Livongo's founding executive team as Chief Commercial Officer, helping take it public in 2019 before its $18.5B sale to Teladoc. He became President of Hinge Health, the digital musculoskeletal care company, in Feb 2021 and helped scale it through its 2025 IPO.
interesting_fact: He was part of Livongo's founding executive team. Livongo went public in 2019 and was bought by Teladoc for $18.5B in 2020, one of the largest digital-health deals ever. He had been an adviser to Hinge before joining it.
deep_cut_fact: He is a former collegiate athlete and said that background drew him to Hinge's mission of transforming chronic pain and musculoskeletal care. He studied Management Science & Information Systems at Penn State before a Kellogg MBA.
notes: Goes by Jim. No published press email was found on Hinge's site (only a support address), so use Hinge Health's investor relations or press page. Low personal media profile.

name: Brian Scott Davis
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Sales and Marketing Officer, Western Digital (since Feb 2025)
profile: B. Scott Davis is a Western Digital lifer with more than 38 years at the company. He led sales in Latin America, the Americas and strategic accounts, then served as SVP of global channel and regional OEM sales. He became EVP and Chief Sales & Marketing Officer in Feb 2025 as WD refocused on HDDs for AI data centers; revenue rose about 44% year on year in fiscal Q4 2026.
interesting_fact: He has spent over 38 years at Western Digital, an unusually long single-company career in the storage industry. He now leads go-to-market as hyperscale AI demand drives the company's growth.
deep_cut_fact: He is a UNC Chapel Hill business graduate (BS Business Administration) and led WD's Latin America sales before running the Americas and strategic accounts.
notes: Goes by Scott Davis. Highly relevant to data-center storage demand (HDD capacity for AI and hyperscalers). Route via WD media relations.

name: Maria Bartiromo
current_role: Business journalist and author. Left Fox News Media in Sept 2026 after 12.5 years; no new role announced as of Nov 2026.
profile: Brooklyn-raised financial journalist (NYU, journalism and economics, 1989) who started at CNN Business. At CNBC from 1993 she became the first journalist to report live from the NYSE floor and won two Emmys. She joined Fox Business/Fox News in 2014 to host Mornings with Maria and Sunday Morning Futures. Fox announced on 3 Sept 2026 that she was no longer with the network.
interesting_fact: Joey Ramone befriended her after the Ramones broke up and wrote a song titled 'Maria Bartiromo', released on his posthumous 2002 solo album 'Don't Worry About Me'.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager at Fontbonne Hall Academy she worked the coat check at her father's Brooklyn restaurant, the Rex Manor. At NYU she interned on Barry Farber's WMCA 570 radio show before landing a CNN internship.
notes: Recently departed Fox (Sept 2026, Fox's decision per NYT), so she is between roles and may be open to new platforms, but tread carefully. Avoid the defamation-litigation topic. Her Wikipedia article carries an 'AI-generated' maintenance tag (Sept 2026); the early-life facts used here predate it. bartiromo.com resolves but shows no content.

name: Whoopi Goldberg
current_role: Moderator/co-host of ABC's The View (since 2007); co-founder of All Women's Sports Network (AWSN)
profile: Born Caryn Elaine Johnson in New York in 1955. She is an EGOT-winning actor and comedian (Emmy, Grammy, Oscar for Ghost, Tony) who broke through with her one-woman show and The Color Purple. She has moderated ABC's The View since 2007 and has business ventures, including co-founding AWSN, an all-women's sports streaming network launched on Pluto TV in 2025.
interesting_fact: She is one of only about 28 people to have won an EGOT. In June 2025 she announced she had co-founded AWSN, a network dedicated entirely to women's sports, streaming on Pluto TV.
deep_cut_fact: Before fame, while living in Berkeley in the 1970s, she worked odd jobs as a bank teller, a bricklayer and a mortuary cosmetologist. Seeing Nichelle Nichols as Uhura on TV as a child sparked her lifelong Star Trek fandom, which later led to her role as Guinan.
notes: Best podcast angle is entrepreneurship: AWSN (women's sports media). Route via ABC/The View press or her talent representation; no published email was found. Couldn't confirm 2026 status on The View beyond late-2025 coverage.
